video-davinci-resolve-mrhvgoq9ly-youtube.title: DaVinci Resolve: Level One Edit & Advanced Techniques for Social Video (Mac & PC)
video-davinci-resolve-mrhvgoq9ly-youtube.summary: This in-depth tutorial switches between DaVinci Resolve’s UI and hands‑on editing, guiding a beginner from a basic Resolve layout and media import to a complete Level One edit and an outline of an Advanced Edit. It covers importing media (including folder-based import), setting up project settings (timeline resolution and vertical formats for social platforms), fundamental timeline editing (blade tool, trim, and basic inspector adjustments), color grading with LUTs (notably a Sony LUT) and color wheels, audio shaping (normalization and compressor), B‑roll insertion and multi‑track layering, transitions (Push, glitch, and other effects), intro text and logo overlays, masking and tracking for background replacement, cloning/ghosting effects, and the process of exporting with options for captions. The video also demonstrates practical workflow tips for social media content, like vertical timelines, punch-ins, and template-based text—culminating in an advanced edit preview before a final render.

video-davinci-resolve-0dm-zyf09rq-youtub.title: URSA Cine Immersive to Apple Vision Pro: Beginner's Guide, On-Set Tips, and Resolve 20.1 Immersive Workflow
video-davinci-resolve-0dm-zyf09rq-youtub.summary: This video guides beginners through the Blackmagic URSA Cine Immersive workflow for Apple Vision Pro, from hardware setup and on-set tips to a complete post workflow in DaVinci Resolve 20.1. It covers camera settings (iris, built‑in NDs, frame rate, shutter angle, and flicker considerations), on-set monitoring and I/O (SDI, timecode, 10G data port), and offloading. The tutorial then dives into immersive editing in Resolve: enabling the Immersive workflow, resolution and proxy choices based on hardware, color management tailored for Vision Pro, and importing Blackmagic RAW. It expands into advanced tools like Edge Blend, Lens Space/LatLong, text graphics in lens space, Fusion tools for removing unwanted elements, and an ASAF-based Ambisonic workflow with head-tracking monitoring using AirPods. Finally, it covers Vision Pro delivery options (AIVU previews, Vision Pro Bundle, ASAF, VR180) and how to stream to multiple Vision Pros, framing the workflow as a practical, end-to-end pipeline from unboxing to a finished immersive video.

video-davinci-resolve-d33f1tktokg-youtub.title: DaVinci Resolve Studio: 10 AI Tools Demonstrated with Timed Techniques
video-davinci-resolve-d33f1tktokg-youtub.summary: This video showcases ten AI-enabled features directly built into DaVinci Resolve Studio, demonstrated in a practical editing workflow. The presenter traverses a workflow from masking and background composite using the Magic Mask (with a Fusion-based setup) to speed up heavy rotoscoping tasks, through AI-powered transcription and keyword-driven editing for efficient referencing, and into automated subtitling. The guide then covers voice-based tools for post-production, including AI voice training for voice conversion and AI voice isolation to clean dialogue, followed by several music-centric AI features for editing and timing. Additional acceleration comes from AI-powered ripple delete for silences, a Smooth Cut transition to bridge gaps, and AI-driven speed warp for retiming video. Across these sections, the video emphasizes saving hours of manual work and enabling rapid iteration when edits require last-minute changes or alignment to music and beats. The transcript anchors each section to exact DaVinci Resolve actions and settings, providing a concrete, timestamped map of the tools demonstrated.
